clue.text: Bill gets accepted, having official recognition

parts.note: AC is the short form of account, a bill to be paid
credited means believed or accepted as true

explanation.surface: A parliamentary bill is passed and so becomes officially recognised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bill' suggests a draft law, but it gives AC, the abbreviation for account.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone accredited holds formal authorisation or official approval from a recognised body.

clue.text: He advocates queen accepting a husband

indicators.note: the queen takes in the next piece, so it sits inside her letters

parts.note: ER is the Latin abbreviation for Elizabeth Regina, a queen
a husband is one kind of spouse

explanation.surface: A man speaks up for a queen who takes a husband.
explanation.definitionFit: One who espouses a cause supports and champions it, so an advocate fits.

clue.text: Sailor capsized when boom shattered — it's hollow-stemmed

indicators.note: a capsized vessel is turned over, so the sailor's letters run backwards in this down light

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a standard crossword sailor

indicators.note: shattered means broken into pieces, so the letters of the boom are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sailor overturns when the boom breaks apart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capsized' turns AB to BA; 'shattered' rearranges BOOM to MBOO.
explanation.definitionFit: This giant grass has woody hollow canes, the classic hollow-stemmed plant.

clue.text: Does wrong, gets lines

indicators.note: doing something wrong suggests the letters of the first word are put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone misbehaves and is given lines as a school punishment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Does' looks like a verb but is the fodder; 'lines' recalls a school punishment, yet means verses.
explanation.definitionFit: Lyric poems are made of verse lines, so lines stands for poems by metonymy.

clue.text: We object, being placed in improper abode. Why? It's of ill repute!

indicators.note: the objective pronoun is set inside the rearranged letters
improper means not in proper order, so the letters of the abode and Why are jumbled

parts.note: the objective form of we is us

explanation.surface: Indignant residents protest at being lodged in a disreputable dwelling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'improper' makes BAWDYHOE and 'being placed in' slots the pronoun in after the O. 'We object' is grammar: the object form of the pronoun, not a protest.
explanation.definitionFit: A brothel is a house with a notorious reputation, described here as a place of ill repute.

clue.text: Treat raw spillage seen in the river

indicators.note: a spillage scatters things, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Untreated sewage has leaked and can be seen in the river.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests pollution; the definition describes the animal by where it is seen.
explanation.definitionFit: This vole lives along riverbanks and swims in the water, so it is often seen in a river.

clue.text: Sharp detectives in US intelligence set-up

indicators.note: the detectives are placed inside the intelligence agency's letters
set up in a down clue means raised, so the agency's letters read upwards

parts.note: the CIA is the Central Intelligence Agency of the US
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department of the British police

explanation.surface: British detectives are planted inside an American spy organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set-up' makes AIC, and 'in' slots the British police detective branch in after the A; 'Sharp' is a taste, not cleverness.
explanation.definitionFit: An acid taste is sour and tart, which is a sharp flavour.

clue.text: Shock caused by teachers' union's uprising

indicators.note: uprising means going upwards, so in this down light the letters read from bottom to top

parts.note: the NUT was the National Union of Teachers in Britain; with the possessive it gives NUTS

explanation.surface: People are shocked by a revolt led by a teachers' union.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' turns NUTS to STUN. The NUT was a British teachers' union.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun someone is to daze or astonish them, a synonym for shock as a verb.

clue.text: She foretold misfortunes — like grit being found in car's parts

indicators.note: these letters are found within the car's rearranged letters
the car is taken to parts, so its letters are rearranged

parts.note: the 's only shows possession or stands for 'is', so it adds no letters: the word before it gives these letters as it is written
as means like, in comparisons
sand is fine grit

explanation.surface: A doom-monger predicted trouble, like grit getting into a vehicle's components.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' makes CRA, and 'being found in' opens it after its first letter; 'misfortunes' points to the Trojan prophetess nobody believed.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend the Trojan princess prophesied disasters that nobody believed.

clue.text: Charm, going topless at fashionable race meeting

indicators.note: going topless means losing the top, so the first letter is dropped

parts.note: a mascot is a lucky charm

explanation.surface: Someone appears topless at a smart racing event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charm' gives MASCOT and 'going topless' drops its M. Royal Ascot is an upmarket English horse-race meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: The Berkshire racecourse holds Royal Ascot, a famously fashionable horse-racing meeting.

clue.text: Figure mob rush out to see

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are disordered, put out of their usual sequence

explanation.surface: A crowd rushes outside to watch something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure' could be a person, but here it is a geometric shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A geometric figure with four equal sides, a diamond shape, is this.

clue.text: China's place in Western Europe

parts.note: read as geography it absurdly puts the Asian country in Europe; really it names a German city famed for its porcelain, called china

explanation.surface: A geographical puzzle about where China belongs in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' seems to be the country, but it is porcelain, made famously near this German city.
explanation.definitionFit: This German city gave its name to fine porcelain, so it is the home of a famous china.

clue.text: Girl's firm provides entertainment

parts.note: Di is a girl's name, short for Diana; with the possessive it gives DIS
Co is the abbreviation for company, a firm

explanation.surface: A young woman's company puts on shows.
explanation.definitionFit: A dance club or party with recorded music is a form of night-time entertainment.

clue.text: So shaped, his parcel is awkward

indicators.note: an awkward arrangement suggests the letters of the two words are out of order

explanation.surface: Someone's round parcel is difficult to handle.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball-shaped object is round, so the clue's So shaped describes something globular.

clue.text: Used to support worker

parts.note: to second a motion is to support it
a hand is a manual worker, as in farm hand

explanation.surface: Someone is used to supporting a labourer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Used to' looks like a phrase about habit, but 'Used' alone is the definition and 'to' a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods previously owned by someone else are described as pre-owned, not new.

clue.text: Lear's wry smiles are bright and penetrating

indicators.note: wry means twisted, so the letters of the king's name with its s are rearranged

parts.note: King Lear, with the possessive s, supplies five letters
beams are broad smiles

explanation.surface: King Lear's sardonic grins are said to be radiant and piercing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wry' rearranges LEARS to LASER; 'are' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Concentrated light from such devices is intense and can cut through materials.

clue.text: But they're not clerks of the course

definitions.text: But they're not clerks of the course

parts.words: But they're not clerks of the course
parts.note: racecourse bookmakers handle money at the track like accountants, yet are not the officials who run the course

explanation.surface: People at a racecourse who handle money are not the officials in charge.
explanation.walkthrough: A clerk of the course is the official managing a British racecourse; bookmakers keep accounts there too.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a formal British term for bookmakers who take bets on horse racing.

clue.text: Gold rating for cooking grilled dish

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: cooking means the letters of rating are worked up into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A top mark is awarded for culinary skill with a grilled meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for cooking' rearranges RATING to GRATIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish topped with breadcrumbs or cheese and browned under the grill is served this way.

clue.text: Slipped quickly indoors and pinched something

definitions.meaning: to nip in is to pop into a place briefly
in dressmaking a garment taken in at the waist is narrowed or gathered

explanation.definitionFit: Popping briefly inside, or narrowing a waistline in tailoring, both use this phrase.

clue.text: Coach industry

definitions.meaning: a stagecoach, particularly in France, was called by this name
industry here means hard work and application

explanation.definitionFit: The word means careful hard work and was also the name of a French public stagecoach.

clue.text: Toiler disposed to belie his nature

indicators.note: disposed means arranged, so the letters of the worker are set in a new order

explanation.surface: A hard worker is inclined to act against his own character.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition leans on the fodder: idling is the opposite of what a hard worker does.
explanation.definitionFit: To dawdle or hang about idly is the opposite of a hard worker's character.

clue.text: Daily thesis

definitions.meaning: a daily is a newspaper printed every day
a thesis is an academic essay or dissertation

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a newspaper and a written academic study presented for discussion.

clue.text: Hand down to father's heir?

parts.note: pa is father; with the possessive it gives PAS
a son is the traditional heir

explanation.surface: Bequeathing an estate to the man's son and heir.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as one question about inheritance; the phrase is split differently.
explanation.definitionFit: To bequeath or transmit something to a successor is to give it on to the next person.

clue.text: Deadlines

parts.note: split as dead plus lines, it means lines of verse written for the dead on a tombstone

explanation.walkthrough: 'Deadlines' looks like time limits, but read as 'dead lines' it means words for the dead.
explanation.definitionFit: An inscription on a tomb consists of lines written in memory of someone dead.

clue.text: Archbishop has to dress up

indicators.note: up in a down clue means the letters read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: to robe is to dress, in ceremonial garments

explanation.surface: An archbishop must get ready by putting on vestments.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ROBE to EBOR, the Latin signature of the Archbishop of York.
explanation.definitionFit: The Archbishop of York signs himself with this abbreviated Latin name for York.

clue.text: Invest capital?

parts.note: read financially it means put money in; militarily, invest means surround a city such as a capital

explanation.walkthrough: 'Invest' means to lay siege in an old military sense, and a capital city is a natural target.
explanation.definitionFit: To surround a city with an army in order to capture it is an old sense of invest.

clue.text: It strikes one as a mild expletive

definitions.meaning: a punch or knock is something that hits a person
an exclamation of mild annoyance, like drat

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a hit or punch and a gentle exclamation of irritation, as in drat.

clue.text: Samuel's teacher is after old boy with daggers drawn

indicators.note: is after means the teacher's name follows the former pupil's letters

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
in the Bible, the priest Eli raised and taught the young Samuel

explanation.surface: A teacher pursues a former pupil with knives drawn.
explanation.walkthrough: In printing, a dagger mark is also called an obelus, plural obeli.
explanation.definitionFit: These are printed dagger-shaped marks used to signal footnotes or doubtful passages.

clue.text: Some lingo newly expressed

indicators.note: newly suggests the letters are made over afresh into a new order

explanation.surface: A fresh piece of vocabulary has been coined.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram and the definition: a coined word is some lingo newly expressed.
explanation.definitionFit: A newly coined word or expression is exactly a piece of language freshly put into use.
